The CI failure looks legitimate.  It is a shellcheck failure in repotest:

```
11:29:38 [1mIn meta-facebook/meta-catalina/recipes-catalina/plat-svc/files/clemente/init-sma line 220:[0m
11:29:38 [0m    if ip link show "$altn" 2>&1 > /dev/null; then[0m
11:29:38 [33m                            ^--^ SC2069 (warning): To redirect stdout+stderr, 2>&1 must be last (or use '{ cmd > file; } 2>&1' to clarify).[0m
11:29:38 
11:29:38 
11:29:38 [1mIn meta-facebook/meta-catalina/recipes-catalina/plat-svc/files/clemente/init-sma line 221:[0m
11:29:38 [0m        echo $(ip link show "$altn" | sed -nE 's/.*(mctpusb[0-1]):.*/\1/p')[0m
11:29:38 [33m             ^-- SC2046 (warning): Quote this to prevent word splitting.[0m
11:29:38 [32m             ^-- SC2005 (style): Useless echo? Instead of 'echo $(cmd)', just use 'cmd'.[0m
```
@jk@ozlabs.org - Do you have any opinion on this?  Is there a way to get the MCTP connection name to be more consistent?

I would suggest something like this:

https://github.com/jk-ozlabs/systemd/commit/346724b5e6c6c3f1845d24e8b675e78ab64a67c5

(if that's useful for you, let me know and I'll propose upstream)

> (if that's useful for you, let me know and I'll propose upstream)

it was useful in general, so I have just sent the PR for that to upstream systemd.
Yes, it is doing what we need. I have updated the patchset to work with the PR.
Can we add comments as to why we need these different options?  A lot of these I don't see anywhere else in the openbmc tree, so I'd like a record of why we have them enabled on this platform.
My apologies. These are actually downstream stuffs that I overlooked. I've removed them and updtated the patchset.
The changes have been made to work with systemd PR #39989.
Please make sure your commits have been rebased whenever you push them up.

My apologies. I'll add that to my standard procedure.
Meanwhile, I have uploaded another version to 
1. avoid skipping the second MCU when the operation or fw version checking failed on the first one.
2. enable pldmd when both MCU failed the fw version checking.
These changes ensure the MCU firmware update can be execute when either of the MCU's firmware is too old to support MCTP bridging.
Why are we considering pldmd "PartOf" another service?  Should this be Requires?

To access ConnectX 8 NICs via MCTP over USB, we need to do so through an MCU that is programed to serve as an MCTP bridge, such device is designed by NVIDIA and named **System Management Agent** (SMA). There are steps to enable and enumerate the bridge (SMA) and its downstream endpoints (CX8s). This involves waiting for the CX8 NICs to be ready (GPIO **CX_BOOT_CMPLT_CX#** from 0 to 1). The process takes time and accessing the endpoints prematurely by pldmd would break it.
The dependencies that you raised questions about are mostly for the same purpose: to prevent pldmd from accessing CX8 endpoints before they are properly enumerated.
The dependeccies are aimed at:
1. preventing pldmd from starting before CX8 endpoints are ready.
2. stopping pldmd on DC power off (since the whole process needs to be rerun after SMA and CX8s rebooted).

The `PartOf` here and in cx-ready.target is used for the second point. They are tied to init-sma, which will be stoped when **RUN_POWER_PG** deasserted.
Quite frankly, I haven’t had much experience on service dependencies and may not apply them elegantly.
Would it be better that I stripped the `PartOf` and just explicitly stop cx-ready.target and pldmd on **RUN_POWER_PG** de-assertion? Could also improve readability this way.
Why Requisite and not Requires?

The goal is to stop pldmd from starting.
In Requires, service manager will simply start cx-ready if it hasn't been already, which defeats the purpose, while in Requisite, the starting of pldmd will fail when cx-ready is not active.
This seems like something PLDM should always be doing and not something we have to install as a separate config snippet.
You are right. I'll remove this.
nit: `${override_dir}`?
Pardon me. I don’t even remember where that came from. I’ll just use the path without assigning it to a variable.
I don't like use of `PartOf`.  It's especially confusing when we have `pldmd` and `cx-ready` both "part of" `init-sma` but then they have additional dependencies between them.

As explained, the `PartOf` is to allow `cx-ready` to be stopped upon stopping `init-sma` and the dependencies between `pldmd` and `cx-ready` is to prevent pldmd from starting before CX8 endpoints are enumerated.
Can we get more of a description here?  What is "sma"?  What is "cx"?  These aren't generally known terms.
Sure. I'll add more details here.
Why does this need to be after EM?  This doesn't have any assurance that the EM configs are populated.

Checking the EM object of CX8 I/O Mezzanine board is another thing I do to determine CX8 readiness and the number of retry has limit. Doing it too early may exhaust the retries.
However, without Requires EM as well, this probably wouldn't even do much?
I'm surprised this isn't oneshot.  Why simple and not exec?

Declaring it as oneshot will block other units during its execution, which resulted in the values of GPIO **CX_BOOT_CMPLT_CX#** not being updated.
There wasn't much consideration on choosing simple or exec other than wanting the service manager to move on as quickly as possible. But I guess that doesn't make much of difference and using exec is generally recommended.
Why do we need `RemainAfterExit` on this and not have it be a one-shot?

Stopping of `init-sma` will have `cx-ready` and `pldmd` to stop due to the use of `PartOf`. The desired time for this to happen is during DC power off when init-sma is explicitly stopped upon **RUN_POWER_PG** de-assertion.
In the future, when sensor values updating is taking over by pldmd, init-sma will exit after endpoint enumeration is done and `RemainAfterExit` will keep its active state.
Why is this file prefixed with a minus?  Why doesn't it have a number prefix?

There was little I can find about the naming convention of link files and this is following what google did ([-bmc-gbmcncsiusb.link](https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-google/recipes-google/ncsi/files/-bmc-gbmcncsiusb.link)). Later I leaned that the number is just about [rule oldering](https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/778790638563885086/1448656439399940277).
I'll add prefix `80` to it.

Is there any plan for systemd or mctp do to this on their own?  It isn't clear why we need a special file for the USB but we don't need one for i2c/i3c typically.

Can you leave some comments here as to why this is done?

Actually, this is because [systemd_257.5.bb](https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/6885cef749dcf64d75a6f0c3a609b5b136bc8df5/poky/meta/recipes-core/systemd/systemd_257.5.bb#L410) disables Predictable Network Interface Names by wiping NamePolicy clean. Changes in [systemd/systemd#39989](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/39989) will have `ID_NET_NAME_PATH` set for MCTP USB devices. Had `99-default.link` has `path` in `NamePolicy` by default, the file wouldn't be needed.
i2c/i3c are different stories though. They are tied to bus number and have been taken care of by kernel drivers ([mctp-i2c](https://github.com/openbmc/linux/blob/adc218676eef25575469234709c2d87185ca223a/drivers/net/mctp/mctp-i2c.c#L865)/[mctp-i3c](https://github.com/openbmc/linux/blob/adc218676eef25575469234709c2d87185ca223a/drivers/net/mctp/mctp-i3c.c#L576))

I'll add comments in the file as well.
Due to the way you've specified dependencies, it seems like this will end up stopping `pldmd` as a side effect.  Why do we want to do that?

As mentioned above, this is intended to prevent intervention from pldmd during CX8 endpoints enumeration after power cycling SMA and CX8.
Again, I'm not holding tight to this design and revision advice are more than welcome.
